metadata.title: Who Fills the Blank? (the Short)
metadata.role: trailer for Minutes of the Meeting: What an AI Is Handed
metadata.note: audio is the clock; cues are on the Whisper word clock; not hand-edited

lines.title: THE BLANK
lines.narration_text: Who fills in the blank? An AI is about to give advice on a stock, and the very last thing it's told is: your action plan must strictly match, and then a blank.
lines.on_screen: from the first frame: the headline "Who fills in the blank?" (the question is the first thing spoken and the first thing read) and, typing in from 0.3 s, paced to the narration, the line `IMPORTANT: Your action_plan.immediate must strictly match "▯▯▯▯".` in two lines of mono type; the blank is ringed in the accent on "a blank". Three empty seat outlines are then drawn under it, one every 0.9 s. Label "Invented stock · sample data".
lines.source_line: "The closing line of the briefing the workflow builds: Build AI Prompt node, Mycroft main @ 8665a9f."

lines.title: THREE VOICES
lines.narration_text: I'm Tanmay Kulkarni, for Humanitarians AI. In an open-source finance pipeline I contributed to, three simulators, I call them voices, each read the same invented stock in their own way.
lines.on_screen: headline "Three voices, one stock". As he says the name, a name line fades in inside the safe area ("Tanmay Kulkarni · Humanitarians AI"). A stock tag lands above the seats: "Ironbridge Power · invented". The seats get their labels, one on each "voice": Sim 1 growth against sentiment, Sim 2 three investors, Sim 3 how close to a change.
lines.source_line: "Mycroft, What-If Simulation Agent recipe; PR #70, merged."

lines.title: THEY DISAGREE
lines.tone: even, then a beat of surprise
lines.narration_text: The first voice weighs the stock's growth against its sentiment, and says strong sell. The second asks how an aggressive investor would see it, and says enter a full position. The third checks how close the verdict is to changing, and says it's fragile: a stability of point oh five.
lines.on_screen: headline "They don't agree". The seats fill on their phrases: STRONG SELL (82%); ENTER FULL POSITION (four limits met, exactly); stability 0.05 with a small gauge near zero.

lines.title: THE WEIGHING
lines.narration_text: They were asked different questions, so a chair weighs them. Forty-five percent for the first, thirty-five for the second, twenty for the third. Together, two point one seven out of five. That's a sell, and the blank fills in.
lines.on_screen: headline "The chair weighs them". The weights land on the seats (45%, 35%, 20%), then the pieces (0.37, 1.75, 0.05), then the total on a one-to-five bar (2.17, in the SELL band). On "the blank fills in", SELL is written into the ringed blank at the top: the loop's payoff.
lines.source_line: "c11, aggregate: weights, pieces, score; bands from the Aggregate node."

lines.title: THE MINUTES
lines.tone: quieter, a little ominous without drama
lines.narration_text: But the AI never heard that meeting. All it gets is the minutes: about four hundred and seventy words, a profile, three simulations, a verdict, and, at the very bottom, the line you just saw.
lines.on_screen: headline "What the AI gets". The three seats fold into a sheet of five stacked sections (profile, three simulations, verdict); the label "about 470 words" arrives; the filled line slides to the sheet's foot and stays last.

lines.title: WHAT THE FULL FILM SHOWS
lines.narration_text: In the full film, I follow that one stock through the whole meeting, and every figure comes from a file you can open. I show what the AI is handed, and what the minutes don't say. And I show the one place where my own copy of these steps disagreed with the original, and how I caught it.
lines.on_screen: headline "In the full film". The sheet moves up and shrinks to the top of the scene; four previews arrive **one at a time** in a preview zone under it (y 920 to 1380, full safe width), each replacing the last: a file tag opens to a path ("simulation-results.json"); the sheet is outlined ("what the AI is handed"); two identical lines appear one after the other ("0.5 typed" and "0.5 filled in", both printed "Sentiment Score: 0.5/1.0"); two boxes "original" and "my copy" with "21 of 23" turning to "23 of 23".
lines.source_line: "The long film: the meeting, the minutes, and my own minute-taker."

lines.title: THE QUESTION
lines.narration_text: So before an AI summarises your next meeting, have you read the minutes? Who had a vote, and how much of one? The full film is Minutes of the Meeting: What an AI Is Handed.
lines.on_screen: headline "Have you read the minutes?" The previews and the sheet recede; the questions arrive one per phrase ("Have you read the minutes?", "Who had a vote?", "How much of one?"); on "The full film is", the closing title overlays inside the safe area ("Minutes of the Meeting: What an AI Is Handed · Humanitarians AI") and SELL dissolves back to a blank, restoring the opening state.
lines.source_line: none needed (the title is the pointer).
